message: docs(runtime): no live prose claims every drain publishes through flush([])

edits.find:
* An empty list is not a cheap flush and is not treated as one. It still derives the snapshot,
   * moves `#sequence` and notifies every batch subscriber, because `#scheduleDrain` calls
   * `flush([])` precisely so a deferred drain publishes what `#pendingSeeds` carried. Emptiness is
   * a project-tier question and `ProjectRuntime.#publishSeeds` owns it. See ADR-080.

edits.find: **Why this is not fixed in `GraphRuntime`.** Short-circuiting `GraphRuntime.flush([])` or `GraphRuntime.invalidate([])` looks like the more general form of the same fix and would delete a working mechanism. `#scheduleDrain` calls `this.flush([])` precisely so that a deferred drain publishes what `#pendingSeeds` carried, and `flush` computes `effectiveSeeds` as the union of its argument and those carried seeds. An empty argument at that layer does not mean nothing to publish; it means publish whatever was queued. The emptiness of a caller's list is a project-tier question, and the project tier is where it already has an owner.

**Superseded in part by [ADR-088](./ADR-088-the-deferred-payload-is-one-closed-value.md), 2026-09-16.** Three mechanics named above moved. `#scheduleDrain` books the drain and `#drainScheduled` is the member that runs it. `#pendingSeeds` was a private set and is now a public getter over one `#pending` payload. And `flush([])` is one of two branches rather than the whole of the drain: since ADR-088 a deferral that carried a frame replays through `flushAtTick`. The decision this paragraph records does not move, and neither does its reason: emptiness is a project-tier question, and `ProjectRuntime.#publishSeeds` still owns it. [Issue #418](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/issues/418).

edits.find: **Why `#scheduleDrain` still spells `flush([])`.** Pointing it at `#flushSeeds` directly is tempting, because it would make a spy on `flush` mean "one caller-stated publication" exactly. It is refused: the drain is scheduled work, nothing guarantees a scheduler cannot run it while a flush is in flight, and the deferral fallback that protects it lives in the public verb. `flush([])` there still means "publish whatever `#pendingSeeds` carried" rather than "publish nothing", which is why an empty caller list remains a project-tier question owned by `ProjectRuntime.#publishSeeds` under ADR-080 and not a short-circuit here.

edits.find: **One case worth naming, and deliberately not fixed here.** `#flushSeeds` releases the booking on every publication, including one no drain scheduled, so a direct `flush` between a booking and the scheduler running it leaves a job outstanding while the phase says none is booked, and the next deferral books a second. Both jobs are harmless, since the second finds `#pendingSeeds` empty and returns. It is a real disagreement between the booking and the scheduler that holds it, it is older than this slice, and repairing it would move behaviour `scheduler-reentrancy` measures. It gets its own issue rather than a quiet correction inside a refactor whose whole claim is that nothing observable moved.

edits.find: **Decision two. A publication assertion reads the seed list, not the call count.** #375 retargeted twenty spies from `invalidate` to `flush` and kept the local name `invalidate`, and ADR-081 priced that move while ADR-082 answered half of its worry correctly: after the split, `flush` is no longer the tick path, so a spy on it sees strictly less than it did. The surviving half is the drain, which publishes through `flush([])`, so `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` asserts "one publication of any origin" while the case around it says "one live write reached the graph once". No affected rig currently leaves a drain pending, which is why all twenty were green and why this is a test-quality finding and not a bug. It is still a case that can go red for a reason it is not about, or stay green because a drain supplied the publication the assertion wanted.

## Superseding a decision

An ADR records what was decided, so an accepted decision is not rewritten when a later slice decides otherwise. Append a bold marker to the paragraph whose claim stopped being true: **Superseded in part by ADR-nnn, YYYY-MM-DD.** when the decision itself moved, or **Refined by ADR-nnn, YYYY-MM-DD.** when the decision stands and only its mechanism, its spelling or its scope moved. Name the sentence that stopped being true, say what replaced it, link the record that decided otherwise, and leave the original sentence in place. The reasoning belongs to the new record; the marker exists only to stop a reader believing the old one is current.

Two things this convention is not. It does not cover live explanatory prose: a source comment, a docblock or a test comment has no historical claim to make, so it is corrected in place rather than annotated, and a docblock that describes a member that no longer exists is a defect rather than a record. And it does not cover a record that contradicts itself in one file, where the paragraph an amendment in the same document already answers is rewritten conditionally and the correction noted, because a reader cannot be asked to work out which half of one document is current. See [issue #418](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/issues/418).
